articleTitle: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence in Customers' Islamic Mobile Banking Using Intention
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: With artificial intelligence (AI) transforming online shopping, understanding its impact on consumer behavior is crucial. This study investigated how AI influences customers' perceived enjoyment, perceived usefulness, and purchase intention through mobile devices. The technology acceptance model and stimulus-organism-response framework provided theoretical grounding. An online survey of 241 Vietnamese online shoppers examined these effects. Results showed AI positively influenced both perceived enjoyment and usefulness. Enjoyment and usefulness perceptions positively affected purchase intention, with enjoyment having a slightly stronger impact. AI also directly increased purchase intention beyond just influencing perceived enjoyment and usefulness. For practice, they highlight the importance of AI in enhancing enjoyment and usefulness perceptions to increase conversion rates. Overall, AI appears to provide an infrastructure facilitating online purchases irrespective of specific perceptions. The research contributes by unpacking AI's multifaceted role in online shopping behavior.

articleTitle: “Aanat” A Micro-Investing Solution Powered by Robo-Advisors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Saving and investing are essential parts of personal finance. This paper presents a possible solution proposed for a local financial institution “Pearl Bank”<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>This is a pseudo name used to anonymize the local Bahraini bank “SICO”. SICO is one of the leading asset managers, brokers, market makers, and investment banks in the region.. The goal is to make saving and investing easy and secure through a user-friendly platform. Research through surveys and interviews revealed that many people struggle to save money due to high living expenses and a lack of financial knowledge. The proposed solution includes an auto-round-up feature that helps users accumulate funds and facilitates investing through robo-advisors on a live trading platform. The aim is to attract new customers by offering auto-saving and auto-investing, allowing users to invest small amounts and withdraw funds as needed.

articleTitle: Blockchain and Real Estate Ownership in Bahrain
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study proposes a framework for transferring property ownership in Bahrain. This study examines the current ownership transfer system and analyzes blockchain technology as an alternative to facilitate real estate business. This exploratory research proposes a blockchain structure for implementing the ownership transfer process in the real estate business. This proposed mechanism brings buyers and sellers together to reduce overall costs, achieve transparency, and ease the process. We employ platform economics to illustrate how blockchain technology can transfer real estate property ownership. This study proposes that new ownership transfer structures adhere to these established pathways to ensure legal compliance and applicability. Failure to do so would render the new transfer structure legally invalid. Therefore, any proposed changes or innovations in the property ownership transfer process must align with existing legal frameworks to ensure their enforceability and legitimacy. The benefit of the platform is that it provides a reliable and smooth process that is secure and virtually impossible to hack or compromise, reducing the transaction cost and providing a sense of security to all stakeholders. Ultimately increasing the willingness to invest in real estate, especially the forging investors. Implementing such technologies helps improve the real estate market's monitoring and boost the stakeholders' confidence.

articleTitle: Identifying Latent Research Themes on ESG Score and Sharia Compliance: Topic Modelling Approach Using Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: These two flavours of responsible investing-Sharia-compliant investing and ESG investing-share much of the same guiding principles, which include advocacy for environmental stewardship and socio-moral business conduct, but the relationship between these practices of responsible investing has been relatively understudied in academic discourse. This study aims to explore the relationship between ESG and sharia compliance. The study uses “ESG score” or “Sharia compliance”. The raw data is collected from various databases like ProQuest (915), Scopus (1040), and Web of Science (214), a total of 2086 abstract data for the analysis. The results show the most occurring words on wordcloud. Inversely least occurring words on TF-IDF. And also shows a correlation graph for word correlation. For the topic and most important theme modelling through Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA). In this study, we can create 7 most important themes/topics around these keywords which are discussed in the result section. This study reveals very important results that will offer considerable insights to scholars, policymakers, and investors in enhancing their understanding of how the two frameworks converge towards further advancement of sustainable and ethical investing methods.

articleTitle: Critical Review of Embedded Insurance: Opportunities, Challenges and Sustainability in the GCC
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This paper presents a critical analysis of the current state of embedded insurance within the insurance sector in GCC. It discusses embedded insurance evolution, analysing its global impact in addition to its growing relevance to GCC countries. Despite its potential within GCC region, the adoption of embedded insurance remains limited to travel insurances bundled with credit cards lacking personalized offerings. The paper further highlights the opportunities with the rising demand for motor and medical insurance within GCC, emphasizing the importance of a robust ecosystem that relies on strategic partnerships and supportive regulations. Additionally, it highlights how embedded insurance can align with sustainability objectives, specifically financial inclusion. The paper highlights data privacy as the key challenge to embedded insurance, reinforcing the need for a robust regulatory framework that protects customers data and foster innovation for successful implementation of this insurance model.

articleTitle: The Effect of Corporate Governance on Financial Performance of Listed Firms in Saudi Arabia
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The study focused on creating a relationship between corporate governance and the financial performance of companies in Saudi Arabia. The research evaluated the relationship between board member compensation and board member size, as well as the company's financial performance. This study aimed to measure financial performance by return on assets and equity, earnings per share, and net profit. In order to evaluate the relationship between corporate governance and the financial performance of the listed companies in the Saudi market. The data used in this research was collected through each company's annual report and board report on Tadawul. This research adopted a quantitative design. The designated population for this study focused on financial and nonfinancial firms in Saudi Arabia from 2014 until 2018. the results indicated there is no significant relationship between board compensation and the firm's financial performance in firms operating in both the financial and nonfinancial sectors. The results further demonstrated no significant link between board size, and the organization's financial performance in financial and nonfinancial sectors. The study recommends that policymakers and the authorities of the Saudi market adjust and review the corporate governance policies related to board compensation and board size in the listed firms in the Saudi market.

articleTitle: Green Finance for Sustainable Development Policy: Pathway to Environmental, Economic and Social Resilience
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Green finance has become a central instrument for realizing sustainable development goals by facilitating investment in various projects delivering environmental protection, social equal opportunity and economic stability. This study examined green investments' significance in elaborating effective sustainable development frameworks. The paper demonstrated the increasing importance of green investments in reducing industry carbon emissions, developing clean energy markets, and supporting resilience. In this context, the paper also presented leading case studies in the MENA and GCC regions. The paper proposed recommendations to enhance green finance's positive contributions and directions for future research.

articleTitle: The Effect of Economic Policy Uncertainty on Corporate Cash Holdings
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Economic Policy Uncertainty plays a significant role in shaping corporate cash management strategies, with firms often adopting a more conservative approach during periods of heightened uncertainty to safeguard their financial stability. In uncertain environments, firms may prefer to maintain higher cash balances to mitigate risks associated with fluctuating market conditions and unforeseen policy changes. This study explores the effects of economic policy uncertainty (EPU), firm size, and debt-equity ratio on corporate cash holdings using a panel dataset of 440 observations from 40 firms over a 10-year period. Employing Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), Fixed Effects, and Random Effects models, the analysis reveals a significant positive relationship between firm size and cash holdings, indicating that larger firms tend to maintain higher cash reserves. Although a positive but statistically insignificant association between EPU and cash holdings suggests that firms may build cash in anticipation of rising uncertainty, no significant effect of the debt-to-equity ratio on cash reserves was identified. Overall, the findings underscore the critical role of firm size and economic conditions in corporate financial management, particularly in the strategic planning of cash reserves.

articleTitle: Nexus Between Inflation, Unemployment, Population and Gross Domestic Product: Evidence From GCC Region
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This research investigates the nexus between inflation, unemployment, population and gross domestic product (GDP) for the GCC countries over the period of 19992023. The data was collected from the World Bank Open Database and analyzed using E-views 12 software. The results find high inflation generally affects economic growth, but effects vary. GDP and unemployment usually have an inverse relationship, while population growth and unemployment impact on the economy are not. Some recommendations are provided to solve the problems include managing inflation, improving job creation, and addressing population growth in the GCC countries.

articleTitle: Challenges in the Application of Partnership Contracts in Islamic Banks: A Theoretical Analytical Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The study investigates the challenges of executing Musharaka, a partnership-based contract in the Islamic banks in Bahrain, aiming at how well it connects with the principles of Maqasid al-Shariah. It also examines similar types of applications used in Pakistan and Oman. Using qualitative research methods, interviews were conducted with ten professionals, including Islamic bankers with more than 15 years of experience and risk professionals who understand the structure of the Musharaka contracts. NVIVO software has been used to analyze the data. Findings demonstrate that the lower embracing of Musharaka contracts is because of challenges like difficulty monitoring, high risk, and lack of awareness among customers and staff. Furthermore, Musharaka contracts have higher levels of risk than other financing techniques. This makes them less favorable to the banks. Neglecting these obstacles, the study demonstrates that Musharaka, with its profit and loss sharing structure, better completes Maqasid al-Shariah's objectives than other contracts such as Murabaha. The study emphasizes the need for policies to improve awareness and decrease the risk of these contracts to improve their adoption. These findings can notify the decision-makers in the Islamic banking sector in Bahrain to execute strategies that improve the usage of Musharaka contracts while connecting with the financial principles of Islam. Moreover, the research offers insights into the implications of applying these contracts in different nations. It provides recommendations to overcome the challenges specific to the banking sector of Bahrain. This study is worthy of both banking professionals and policymakers as it will help to find the extent of Islamic finance practices.

articleTitle: Green Finance on Islamic Financial Markets: A Sustainable Approach to Growth
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The intersection of green finance and Islamic financial markets offers significant potential for promoting sustainable economic growth, especially as environmental and social concerns gain prominence globally. This paper examines the alignment between green finance, which focuses on investments that advance environmental sustainability, and the ethical foundations of Islamic finance, which advocate responsible resource management. By exploring the integration of sustainability principles in Islamic finance, assessing regulatory frameworks, and presenting case studies of successful green projects funded through Islamic mechanisms, this study highlights the opportunities and challenges within these markets. Ultimately, it aims to demonstrate how Islamic green finance can drive sustainable development while adhering to Shariah principles, contributing to a more inclusive and environmentally responsible financial ecosystem.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Mazaya Social Housing Program Using Application Programming Interface Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: In this paper, we examine the challenges faced by social housing applicants and beneficiaries in Bahrain since it was initiated. To achieve this objective, we have conducted a survey and several interviews. The results show a significant need for a comprehensive integration among Mazaya's major stakeholders. Lengthy application procedures and limited access to extensive information for beneficiaries were highlighted as the main challenges of the current scheme. The results also highlight the areas that can be improved by utilizing a proposed mobile application, leveraging open-finance technologies to streamline mortgage processing, and enhancing the overall user experience.

articleTitle: Cashback Savvy Providing Modernize Islamic Banking
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Financial sector has been experiencing significant growth, driven by digital transformation and consumer behavior shifts. In addition, Bahrain and GCC governments are inspiringly and encouraging to create innovative Islamic financing products and Fintech apps. However, the challenge is always that these products are merely a replication of traditional products. Another challenge that is faced by Islamic finance industry is the customers' weak level of Islamic finance literacy which hinder many of them from leveraging products. Financial institutions should remedy these challenges by exploring innovative strategies to maximize customer centric service. We propose in this paper a new financial product/service that leverages existing Islamically compliant services and products. The solution eases the financial burden of customers as well as provide monetary rewards and Takaful benefits.

articleTitle: What is the Role of Zakat and Stable Prices in Narrowing Inequalities in Indonesia?
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The full potential of zakat has yet to be fully utilized, and inequality has increased among the Indonesian population over the last two decades. This study employs the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model to examine the influence of time impacts of zakat, gold prices, exchange rates, and oil prices on inequality in Indonesia. The results suggest that zakat can reduce disparities in the long and short term. Conversely, increasing gold prices, exchange rates, and oil prices can exacerbate inequality. The findings implied that the government and policymakers should improve zakat management, public trust, technology, and information systems to enhance zakat distribution. Additionally, since rapid responses to price shocks through inflation can negatively affect the ability of the poor and vulnerable to meet their basic needs, maintaining price stability is crucial.

articleTitle: Uplifting Brothers, Islamic Peer to Peer Lending with Cashback
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Recently, peer-to-peer (P2P) lending has gained widespread popularity worldwide. However, most of the P2P lending apps are designed to cater for corporate clients' needs and requirements. This paper aims to design a Fintech app for retail customers to re-innovate the traditional lending relationship. The app will ensure that borrower repays only the principal amount, while a profit is being generated by investing installments in Wakala deposits. This approach not only addresses the gap in the current market but also aligns with Islamic financial principles, offering a sustainable and profitable solution for all stakeholders involved. This aligns with Vision 2030 goals as it promotes savings practices, entrepreneurship, innovation, economic diversity, and financial inclusion. A survey was conducted to investigate the characteristics and readiness of retails customers for such a solution.

articleTitle: The Pandemic's Price Tag: Agricultural Inflation and Its Drivers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Since the onset of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, significant disruptions have occurred in global economies. This study focuses on the imbalance between supply and demand within the agricultural sector. The analysis period was chosen to align with the start and end of the vaccination campaign, which began in late 2020 and concluded on August 31, 2021. To analyze the data, an Auto Regressive Distributed Lags (ARDL) model was applied. A pre- and post-analysis was performed to assess key factors, including unit roots, variance inflation, multi-collinearity, heteroscedasticity, cointegration, and structural breaks, which were tested using cumulative sum analysis. The results highlight the relationship between demand-side factors and their influence on the agricultural index. Additionally, the economic stimulus policy showed contrasting behavior when compared to the agricultural index. These insights may provide a foundation for future research and guide policy decisions.

articleTitle: Sharia Governance of Islamic Banks and Islamic Windows in the Kingdom of Bahrain
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The purpose of this research paper is to compare the Sharia governance laws of Islamic windows and Islamic banks in the Kingdom of Bahrain. It also examines the strength of these laws from both theoretical and practical perspectives by interviewing employees in the Sharia departments of Islamic windows. The goal is to determine whether the Sharia governance laws applied to Islamic windows differ from those of Islamic banks and if they require further development.

articleTitle: Investigating Relationship Between Working Capital Management and Shareholder's Wealth: Evidence from USA
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Over the past few decades, there have been major developments in capital management and wealth creation, yet the relationship between them is not clear. This study attempts to fill this gap by examining the relationship between working capital management and shareholder wealth for Dow Jones Index in USA for the period 2014 to 2023. Return on Invested Capital (ROC) and Return on Average Common Equity (ROE) was used as an indicator for shareholder wealth whereas, Average Inventory Days, Receivables Collection Days, and Inventory Turnover were used as indicator for working capital management. The key findings suggest that there is a strong relationship between inventory days and return on invested capital. Significant positive relationship between cash conversion cycle and return on equity, significant relationship between inventory turnover and return on equity. Recommendations include optimizing working capital techniques, balancing capital usage, and monitoring key metrics for enhanced profitability and shareholder value. Regular analysis of working capital components is crucial for informed decision- making.

articleTitle: Exploring Digital Village Development for Circular Economy: A Case Study of Padaringan Village-Owned Enterprise, Langonsari, Bandung Regency, Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This article examines the Village-Owned Enterprise (BUMDES) Padaringan, Bandung Regency, which is developing a digital business in the face of the digital economy and industry. Digitalization carried out by BumDes Padaringan is the process of using digital technology to change business models and provide new income and value-generating opportunities, or it can be referred to as the move to a digital business. Researchers used a qualitative method with a case study approach to see and analyze how village-owned enterprises carry out digital transformation in developing business lines as one of the industry players. Langonsari village, located in the Pameungpeuk sub-district, is a rural area with natural potential and a garment industry, making it an area with urban and rural community types. The economic potential in Langonsari village, in addition to businesses in handicrafts, Peci and Sundanese Iket, clothing, and culinary business, is also the potential for hilly natural tourism. The management of BUMDES Padaringan strives to make a healthy and highly credible digital company and become a digital village model. With the support of digital marketing research and development and effective and efficient marketing communication strategies, the community's economic potential in Langonsari village is expected to develop. This research seeks to identify the potential of BUMDES in developing digital marketing business activities, including marketing in the marketplace, creating product photo and video studios, and podcast activities to become a forum for the existence of village and BUMDES activities. The research reveals a model of digital marketing communication.

articleTitle: Impact of Inflation, Interest Rates, and Unemployment on us Stock Market Returns
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study performs econometric approaches to investigate the effects of inflation, interest rates, and unemployment rates on U.S. stock market returns from January 2000 to June 2024. According to the research, nominal earnings of stocks increase, and corporations can pass on greater costs to customers, which suggests that equities could act as a hedge against inflation. Interest rates indicate higher borrowing costs for businesses and lower profitability, which is expected to negatively impact stock returns. Nonetheless, there is an unexpectedly strong positive link between unemployment rates and stock market performance. The study provides investors and policymakers with crucial new information, considering the intricacy of the relationships between different macroeconomic conditions and stock market performance. It emphasizes the significance of considering outside variables, such as changes in policy, which could affect anticipated economic linkages. Based on sector-specific effects and comparative evaluations in other economies, further study could build upon these findings.

articleTitle: Intellectual Capital Practices in ASEAN Islamic Banks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The ASEAN region's Islamic banking institutions' reporting policies on intellectual capital were discovered in this study. It is becoming more widely acknowledged that intellectual capital―which includes relational, structural, and human capital―is a strategic asset that enhances the viability and performance of Islamic banks. Given the growing importance and strategic role of Islamic banks, these institutions are expected to have strong intellectual capital based on knowledge and experience derived from Sharia. However, despite its significance, intellectual capital reporting has yet to become a consistent practice across Islamic banks in ASEAN. Using a qualitative descriptive methodology, this study looks at the annual reports of a number of the top Islamic banks in the area. The findings reveal considerable variability in intellectual capital disclosure, influenced by factors such as national regulations, bank size, and commitment to good governance. These results suggest the need for standardized intellectual capital reporting in the ASEAN Islamic banking sector to enhance transparency and global competitiveness. A unified reporting framework would promote greater clarity and accountability, ultimately strengthening the global position of Islamic finance.

articleTitle: Foreign Financial Inflows, Islamic Banking, and Poverty Alleviation in Sub-Saharan African Countries
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The study examines the impact of foreign financial inflows on poverty alleviation in sub-Saharan Africa, by considering Islamic banking as a sustainable alternative, using panel ARDL estimations over 31 years (1991–2021), and focusing on ten African countries. The study proxies foreign financial inflows with official development assistance (ODA), external debts, diaspora remittances, and Islamic finance instruments. Household consumption serves as a proxy for poverty alleviation. The results reveal that ODA (p = 0.0006, coefficient = 0.202311) and diaspora remittances (p = 0.0000, coefficient = 0.398084) positively impact poverty alleviation, while external debts (p = 0.2658, coefficient =-0.036205) have a detrimental effect. Due to its interest- free and risk-sharing principles, Islamic banking offers a sustainable alternative to conventional financial systems, reducing poverty without fostering economic dependency.

articleTitle: The Impact of Corporate Social Responsibility on Financial Distress Risk: Evidence from GCC Countries
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This research seeks to explore the impact of corporate social responsibility (CSR) on financial distress risk (FDR) using a regression model on a sample of data taken from publicly traded non-financial companies in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) country's stock markets from the period 2018-2022. The dependent variable (i.e., FDR) is assessed using the Altman Z-Score model, and the findings of this research indicate a significant and positive link between a company's financial distress risk and corporate social responsibility activities. The findings support the argument that sustaining CSR practices during financial distress may be considered a strategic decision to protect long-term ties and support, which are critical to the company's rehabilitation and future prosperity. The results of this study can assist GCC-listed firms to become more conscious of the aspects that might improve their CSR activities and take the required safeguards to maintain their financial situation, avoid financial distress risks, and lengthen the firm's continuity.

articleTitle: Cognitive Bias and Sustainable Decision-Making: A Bibliometric Analysis of Emerging Trends and Research Gaps
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This paper reviews articles that have been published between 2001 and September 2024 with the emphasis on the impact of cognitive biases on sustainable decisions. By adhering to the PRISMA protocol, the authors analyzed 124 articles set in the WOS and Scopus databases. The results indicate that there is still relatively little empirical evidence and theoretical literature on cognitive biases, such as overconfidence, optimism, narcissism, and their impacts on sustainability performance. In this respect, the study calls for more interdisciplinary studies to connect psychology, corporate strategy, and environmental sciences to produce a more profound understanding of how biases influence sustainability. The bibliometric analysis shows the direction of the research development where the four most productive countries are the US, China, Germany, and India. The study recommends future research combining cognitive psychology with sustainability studies for constructing more inclusive theoretical frameworks to comprehend how and when biases influence sustainable environmental policies and initiatives.

articleTitle: The Effect of Risk Management Activities on the Performance of Conventional and Islamic Banks in Bahrain
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study examines the impact of risk management activities on the financial performance of a selected number of conventional and Islamic banks in Bahrain during the period 2018–2022. Fixed effects models reveal capital risk, credit risk, liquidity risk, efficiency, and leverage significantly influence bank profitability. Specifically, higher capital adequacy and NPL ratios reduce profitability, reflecting constraints and losses from excess capital and deteriorating asset quality. Greater liquidity risk increases ROA but has no significant effect on ROE. Higher cost efficiency lowers profitability, implying a potential overemphasis on cost reduction. The findings suggest banks should develop risk management frameworks tailored to their business models to optimize the risk-return tradeoff.

articleTitle: The Economic Impact of Financial Transfers from Expatriates in GCC Countries on Islamic Developing Nations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The current study examines the impact of expatriates' financial transfers from Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries on economic growth, using panel data from nine Islamic developing nations: Nigeria, Egypt, Pakistan, Algeria, Bangladesh, Sudan, Senegal, Tunisia, and Afghanistan, covering the period from 1990 to 2022. The study adopts both descriptive analytical approach and econometric techniques. The analysis reveals a significant error term in the remittance data, which means that there is a cointegration between financial transfers and economic growth. Additionally, the study identifies a bidirectional causality between these two factors. Accordingly, the study recommends that policymakers in the countries studied develop and implement strategies to optimize the benefits of remittances, ensuring their effective use to foster economic development and improve standards of living.

articleTitle: Fintech Innovations in Assessing SME Creditworthiness in Bahrain
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Access to finance is a critical determinant of success for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). According to the Bahrain Economic Development Board, SMEs in the Kingdom of Bahrain faced significant challenges in securing necessary financial resources as of 2008. This paper proposes integrating a real-time alternative data credit scoring API with existing credit report services. By utilizing machine learning for credit scoring, this solution enables financial institutions and Export Bahrain to make informed lending decisions and efficiently handle risks. By incorporating machine learning for credit scoring, this solution helps the financial institutions and Export Bahrain make informed decisions on lending while mitigating risks effectively. A mixed-method approach, surveys, and interviews were used in the study, with a sample of 63 SME owners participating in the survey. The proposed solution aims to bridge the gap in the financing of SMEs by applying alternative data sources for real-time credit scoring, enabling SMEs to access more reliable financial services. This, in turn, is expected to foster their growth and increase their contribution to the overall economic well-being of the region.

articleTitle: The Impact of Exchange Rates and Inflation on the International Trade of GCC Countries
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This research paper examines the critical influence of exchange rate fluctuations and inflation on the dynamics of international trade within the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries. By analyzing the relationship between the macroeconomic factors, the study aims to provide insights into how currency stability and price levels impact trade competitiveness and economic integration in the region. The results show that the exchange rate plays a crucial role for international trade for GCC countries as the currency is pegged with US dollars. Furthermore, it was also found that the rise in inflation has impacted the businesses in GCC countries. The findings of this research contribute to a deeper understanding of the economic policies needed to enhance trade performance and sustain growth in the GCC economies.

articleTitle: The Effects of Perceived Benefits and Ease of Use on the Reuse Intention of Islamic Banking QRIS through Satisfaction Among Culinary MSMEs: Does Fintech Literacy play a role?
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Banda Aceh, with 9,591 MSMEs, benefits from QRIS in enhancing transactions and supporting financial inclusion, but faces challenges such as limited digital literacy and internet connectivity issues, which may hinder its continued use. This study examines the impact of perceived benefits and ease of use on the reuse intention of culinary MSMEs in Banda Aceh using BSI QRIS, exploring the mediating role of satisfaction and the moderating role of fintech literacy. Data from 105 MSMEs were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), revealing that perceived benefits positively influence satisfaction and reuse intention, while satisfaction does not mediate the relationship. Fintech literacy moderates the relationship between perceived benefits, ease of use, and reuse intention. The study's findings suggest that it's critical to raise perceived benefits and ease of usage to enhancing satisfaction and fintech literacy, so that culinary MSME players in Banda Aceh City can continue to use the BSI QRIS payment system repeatedly.

articleTitle: Environment, Social and Governance (ESG) and Asset Quality of Banks in the Gulf Cooperation Council
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study investigates the relationship between Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) scores and asset quality within the banking systems of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries. A total of 42 banks including conventional and Islamic banks were selected for the study. The primary dependent variables include non-performing loans and the impaired percentage of shareholders' equity, while the independent variable is the management score derived from ESG criteria. Regression analysis was employed to assess the relationships between these variables. The study results revealed a significant relationship between management scores and asset quality, indicating that higher management scores correlate with lower non-performing loans. In addition, a negative correlation was observed between non-performing loans (as a percentage of shareholders’ equity) and key performance indicators such as earning assets, market capitalization, and return on average common equity.

Author Keywords: assets quality and Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC

articleTitle: Investigating Entrepreneurial Motivation and Intention Among Indonesian Youths: Integrated the Theory of Planned Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Indonesia lags behind neighboring countries in entrepreneurial activity despite one-third of its youth aspiring to be entrepreneurs. The government aims to increase the number of aspiring entrepreneurs by one million by 2024. To achieve this, the government and businesses need to implement effective entrepreneurial motivation plans and policies to support the development of new innovative ideas. Entrepreneurship is crucial in driving a country's economic growth, promoting employment opportunities, enhancing income distribution, and ultimately contributing to improving community welfare. This study analyzes the Indonesian youth's entrepreneurial motivation and intention. Data was gathered from 400 respondents through the utilization of convenience sampling. The evaluation of the model, the credibility, and the validity of the data were evaluated using confirmatory factor analysis, while structural equation modeling was employed to test the hypotheses. The findings reveal that ability, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, and opportunity positively and significantly impact entrepreneurial motivation, which positively and significantly influences entrepreneurial intention. Conversely, attitude has been found to exert a positive but insignificant effect on entrepreneurial motivation. This study provides valuable insights for managers and practitioners to develop effective strategies for fostering innovation within SMEs. It addresses the intentions of student entrepreneurs to continue or withdraw from pursuing entrepreneurship, offering a unique perspective.

articleTitle: Linking Islamic Moral Economics and Circular Economy: A Pathway to Sustainability
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study delves into the simultaneous exploration of the circular economy and Islamic moral economics to uncover how the circular economy can be integrated with Islamic moral economics. It examines the methodology and sources of Islamic moral economy, highlights the distinctions between Islamic economics and capitalist economy, and presents empirical evidence. The research reveals that Islamic moral economy and the circular economy are mutually supportive concepts that can collaborate towards establishing a more sustainable and equitable world. Specifically, Islamic moral economy and the circular economy can be linked through sustainable agriculture, efficient water usage, and fair trade. Hence, policymakers must prioritize the circular economy to positively influence environmental sustain ability within Islamic nations and globally. A socio-cultural setting grounded in shared beliefs and perspectives, where individuals can discover spiritual validation for practices like reducing, reusing, recovering, recycling, and refusing, as well as other principles of circularization, will offer them more profound motivation compared to the role of producers and consumers in a contemporary market-driven society.

articleTitle: Beyond Tradition: The AI Frontier in Portfolio Management
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) revolutionizes portfolio management, offering unparalleled data processing and analytical capabilities that significantly enhance decision-making processes. AI's ability to analyze vast amounts of traditional and alternative data, including social media sentiment, news feeds, and satellite imagery, allows for discovering intricate patterns and connections that often elude human investors. This technological advancement facilitates more informed and strategic investment decisions, improving risk management through precise identification and quantification of risk factors, and enabling dynamic asset allocation to optimize portfolios. AI-driven algorithmic trading ensures efficient execution of trades, capitalizing on market opportunities with precision and speed. Personalized investment strategies are crafted by AI, considering individual risk tolerance, financial goals, and investment horizons, thus catering to specific investor needs.

articleTitle: Integrating Guillain-Barré Syndrome Awareness with Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance: A Path Towards Enhanced Health and Well-being
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) is an uncommon and a potentially lethal autoimmune ailment in which the immune system assaults peripheral nerves, causing signs generally including weakness and respiratory failing. This study investigates the relationships between demographic characteristics of age, education, gender, prior knowledge and personal experience to awareness of Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS) with the emphasis on 8 hypotheses related to these characteristics. The study both emphasizes the need to include Islamic principles in educational endeavors and the contribution of the financial institutions to community health programs. These results are consistent with Sustainable Development Goal 3, which seeks additional health education and awareness to improve outcomes for people with GBS.

articleTitle: Forecasting Nvidia Stock Trends: An Analytical Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Nvidia stocks have experienced significant volatility and growth in recent years, largely driven by the company's leadership in the graphics processing unit (GPU) market and its pivotal role in the booming sectors of artificial intelligence and gaming. The surge in demand for AI technologies has positioned Nvidia as a key player, with its GPUs being essential for machine learning and data processing tasks. This strong market position has led to soaring stock prices, attracting investors’ attention, and boosting the company's market capitalization. However, potential investors should be mindful of factors such as market competition, regulatory changes, and the cyclical nature of the tech industry, which could influence Nvidia's future performance. Against this backdrop, we tried to forecast the stock trends of Nvidia using time series models.

articleTitle: Green and Renewable Energy Impact on Sustainable Indices: Empirical Study on Selected Indian Stocks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Renewable natural resources based on power and energy, such as solar, wind, and hydropower energy, play a vital role in mitigating the impact of environmental degradation and climate change. This paper examines the effect of BSE Greenex, BSE Carbonex, and BSE 100 ESG on selected green energy stocks. This study comprises the time series data from Dec, 2020 to Sept 2024 by using multiple regression and event window of volatility analysis. Result shows there is a significant impact observed with stocks like NTPC, ADNA, and BFUT. However, the impact is not very high with KPEN and WAAS. These results raise awareness of renewable energy as a key factor improving financial performance, energy security, and sustainable development. Furthermore, the paper underlines the need to mobilise more capital for innovation in green technology, supportive policies as well as advancements in energy storage as well as distribution networks to increase the adoption of renewable energy. This change is indeed going to be strategic in the promotion of sustainable long-term growth economically and in the fight against the world's environmental crises.

articleTitle: Maqasid Al-Shariah and Green Finance: A Theoretical Framework on Islamic Finance with Sustainable Development Goals for a Greener Future
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The study investigates incorporating Islamic financial concepts with green finance to advance sustainable development. Maqasid al-Shariah, the guiding principle of Islamic finance, prioritizes ethical investing, social welfare, and asset preservation through Shariah-compliant instruments, including sukuk, zakat, and waqf. These instruments can be utilized to fund projects that promote both environmental sustainability and social responsibility. This integration fulfills Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), specifically in clean energy, sustainable cities, climate action, and responsible consumption. The integrated approach guarantees a sustainable global financial landscape by promoting long-term economic stability, environmental protection, and social welfare. It encompasses a comprehensive framework for achieving sustainability. This study provides a theoretical model to emphasize the immense potential of Islamic finance in substantially contributing to the broader, more comprehensive green finance agenda.

articleTitle: The Impact of Profit Rate, Sharia Committee, Leverage, Profit Growth, Cash Flow, and BI Rate on the Issuance of Sukuk Types in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of the rate of return, Sharia Committee, leverage, profit growth, cash flow, and the BI Rate on sukuk issuance in Indonesia. The research utilizes a quantitative approach with secondary data from 34 companies and 73 sukuk types (ijarah and mudharabah) issued between 2012 and 2021. The findings reveal that 34.94% of sukuk issuance is explained by the independent variables, with significant effects from the Sharia Committee, leverage, and cash flow. Meanwhile, the rate of return, profit growth, and BI Rate show no significant influence. The Sharia Committee emerges as the most influential factor. The study concludes that companies must ensure compliance with Sharia principles, carefully manage their financial obligations, and maintain good cash flow management to enhance investor interest. The remaining 65.06% of sukuk issuance is likely driven by factors not included in this study, such as profitability and corporate governance, indicating potential areas for future research.

articleTitle: The Role of Customer Satisfaction in Mediating Effects of CSR and Islamic Service Quality on the Islamic Banking Customer's Loyalty in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This research investigates the encouragement of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and Islamic service quality on customer loyalty in Bank Syariah Indonesia (BSI) in Banda Aceh, Indonesia, with customer satisfaction acting as a mediator. Primary data were gathered from 126 customers of BSI employing a purposive sampling method and subsequently assessed with Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The outcomes indicate that CSR and Islamic service quality do not exert significant direct effects on customer loyalty; however, they do have a positive influence on customer satisfaction. Additionally, customer satisfaction comprehensively mediates the connection between CSR, Islamic service quality, and customer loyalty. This underscores the necessity of enhancing CSR practices and the quality of Islamic services to boost customer satisfaction, which subsequently cultivates customer loyalty within the Islamic banking sector. These insights suggest that by focusing on these factors, BSI and similar Islamic banks can build stronger relationships with customers, thereby reinforcing loyalty and strengthening the involvement of CSR and quality service in the Islamic banking segment

articleTitle: Necessary and Sufficient Conditions in the fsQCA to Adopt and Use Benefitpay in Bahrain
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The disposition of mobile payments has gained some strong pedigree globally and research that explores these mobile payments adoption and use is increasing. Using the fuzzy set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) model, we analyzed how configurational antecedents of TAM led to adopting and using BenefitPay in Bahrain. The empirical analysis establishes that low perceived risk, high perceived usefulness, high perceived ease of use, high compatibility, old age, and high income are necessary and sufficient conditions to adopt and use the BenefitPay mobile payment application. Furthermore, it is revealed that high perceived risk, low compatibility, low perceived usefulness, low income, perceived ease of use, and young people are sufficient conditions for the non-use of BenefitPay. Users assess the benefits to be derived from BenefitPay before they adopt and use it. This research is significant as it calls for the providers of mobile payment Apps to enhance their security, cost-effectiveness, trust, and convenience.

articleTitle: Development of Indonesian Islamic Banking Financial Inclusion Strategy: A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Islamic banking in Indonesia has a lower financial inclusion index and profitability than the total banking industry, despite its continuous growth. With better resilience to the crisis, the importance of financial inclusion to the economy, and the dependence on financing income, Islamic banking should increase profitability and play an important role in increasing financial inclusion through financing growth. Despite being widely discussed, predictive analytics with machine learning has not been commonly used in developing banking strategies. This study introduces the use of predictive analytics with machine learning to develop strategies for increasing and aligning the financial inclusion and profitability of Islamic banks in Indonesia through financing, with financial analysis as a feedback mechanism. The study results in the strategy recommendation for Islamic banking to focus on MSME and Consumer financing to increase financial inclusion and profitability concurrently. The research also demonstrates that predictive analytics with machine learning and financial analysis can be used in developing financial inclusion strategies for Islamic banks, with the need for intervention to grow MSME working capital financing. The study is expected to become a new reference in developing strategies to increase Islamic banking's financial inclusion and profitability.

articleTitle: Optimizing Knowledge Management, Innovation, and Competence for Sustainable Organizational Development
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study explores how Knowledge Management, Innovation, and Competence impact Sustainable Organizational Development at PT PLN (Persero) Aceh Regional Main Unit, using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with data from 277 employees. The findings reveal that Knowledge Management significantly affects Innovation (75.3%) and Competence (81.2%), but does not directly impact Sustainable Organizational Development. Instead, its influence is mediated through Innovation and Competence. Innovation and Competence, in turn, significantly contribute to Sustainable Organizational Development, with Innovation at 34.0% and Competence at 56.6%. This indicates that while Knowledge Management is important, organizations must also focus on enhancing Innovation and Competence to achieve long-term sustainability. To ensure effective outcomes, organizations should integrate Innovation and Competence into strategic planning and continuously monitor their impacts.

articleTitle: Understanding Public Perceptions of Digital Sharia Pawnshops in Indonesia: A Sentiment Analysis with Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study aims to identify public sentiment toward digital sharia pawnshop application in Indonesia. This research uses a qualitative method with a sentiment analysis approach with the help of orange data mining. The data used are reviews of the Pegadaian sharia digital application from the google play store taken from January 1, 2022 to January 1, 2024. The total review data used in this study is 2.786 reviews. The results showed that the three most frequently occurring words are “aplikasi”, ‘‘pengguna’, and “Google. In addition, reviews are dominated by statements that have positive (1,258 reviews) where there are various words describing the beneficial features provided by the app such as “emas', “membantu”, “tabungan”, “transaksi”, “cepat”, and ‘‘pembayaran’. On the other hand, there are also some words that have a tendency to have negative sentiments (794 reviews) such as “error”, “susah”, dan “gagal”. This research is limited by the use of google play store review data from three years ago, before the release of Pegadaian sharia digital application. For future research, researchers advise reidentifying the sentiment of the Pegadaian sharia digital application after 3 years, 4 years, etc., to compare sentiment changes.

articleTitle: Evaluating Financial Performance of Islamic and Conventional Banks in UAE: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The present research is an effort to analyze the Islamic and conventional banks “performance through ratios in UAE., covering the time period from 2011 to 2023. The data has been retrieved from BankFocus data base. The paper investigates the corollary of the ratios such as Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR)., Total Assets (TA)., Loan to Deposit Ratio (LDR)., Cost to Income Ratio (CIR) and Net Interest Margin (NIM) on banks” (IBs & CBs) performance in terms of ROAA and ROAE. The panel data regression has been applied to obtain the desired outcomes. The findings indicate that CIR and NIM have both negative and positive impact on ROAA and ROAE of IBs in UAE. In addition., the panel results for CBs in UAE show a positive and significant impact of CAR and NIM on both ROAA and ROAE. In contrast T A and CIR show a significant negative effect in this context.

articleTitle: Digital Influence on Entrepreneurship: Impact on Mindset and Small Business Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study, we investigate how digital technologies are changing the entrepreneurial mindset and minor business operations in Bahrain. With the advent of digital tools like cloud service, e-commerce platforms, and social media, small businesses in Bahrain are increasingly relying on these technologies to enhance their competitiveness and productivity. The introduction of new digital technologies has led to an entrepreneurial mindset that has a distinct flavor of innovation, agility and data-based management. This shapes how entrepreneurs control and consequently how well they are able to operate their companies. This paper explores the transformation of the national entrepreneurial spirit and small businesses in Bahrain, with the country trying to reconcile constraints on its resources that are inhibiting growth by competing globally. The key issue of this survey is how entrepreneurs in Bahrain are challenged by the advent to digital technology when their resources are limited- restricting them from taking traditional growth paths for a modern business.

articleTitle: Robo Advisors Revolution: Transforming Landscape of Mutual Fund Investments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Robo-advisors have simplified mutual fund investing by making financial planning, including personalized investment plans, accessible to a much wider audience. In this paper, we will explore the role of robo-advisors in mutual fund investing, which has elements of democratizing financial services by providing expert advice traditionally available only to high-net-worth individuals due to cost-effectiveness and scalability through automation. Current study applies modern behavioral finance algorithms and principles that reduce common investor decision biases such as loss aversion and overconfidence. Robo-advisors can provide tax-optimized and diverse personalized investment strategies. In this study, we compare the portfolio composition, risk-adjusted returns, and self-directed investment management paths of robo-advisors with those of those who received human advice. We explore the impact on investor behavior, financial literacy, and broader market dynamics using Vanguard's Personal Advisory Service (P.A.S.), one of the world's leading robo-advisors. Robo-advisors can help improve social welfare by lowering the cost of advisory services and reducing the impact of cognitive biases on decision-making, thereby providing users with superior mutual fund investment opportunities.

articleTitle: Portfolio Optimization of Sharia-Based Stocks Using Deep Learning: A Case of Bahrain Bourse
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Optimizing portfolios consists of finding the most efficient allocation of funds amongst selected assets. Since the advent of technology in recent years, the process of optimizing such portfolios has undergone substantial evolution driven by integrating machine learning and incorporating complex problem elements to more accurately reflect real-life scenarios. This paper studied solving such a problem using genetic algorithm based on downside mean-variance model that was applied on Sharia-complaint stock listed on Bahrain Bourse. Researchers used the daily closed stock prices between April 2015 and April 2023 to calculate the daily returns and fed them into the algorithm to find the optimal fund allocations amongst the 13 stocks of the Bahrain Islamic Index (BIX). The resulted optimized portfolio performance was then compared with the BIX and mean-variance portfolios using the cumulative daily returns along with Sharpe and Sortino ratios, which all confirmed that the study's model offered higher daily returns for one unit of risk. The results also revealed that the performance of the study's portfolio outperformed the others during COVID-19 pandemic which proved its ability to mitigate systematic risk caused by global crises.

articleTitle: The Effects of Return and Risk Perception, Investment Decision, and Intergenerational on Reinvestment Intention to the Islamic Capital Market: Mediation-Moderation Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study aims at examining the effect of return and risk perceptions, investment decisions, and intergenerational on reinvestment intention to Islamic capital market among investors in Banda Aceh city, Indonesia. Of 20,918 Islamic capital market investors in the city, 125 of them were selected as the research sample using a combination of purposive sampling and proportionate stratified random sampling techniques. The research collected primary data through the distribution of questionnaires and conducted an Analysis Moment of Structural- Structural Equation Modelling (AMOS-SEM). The study found that return perception positively influences investment decision but has no effect on reinvestment intention. Conversely, risk perception has no influence on investment decisions but positively affects reinvestment intention. Unlike investment decisions that fully mediate the return perception-reinvestment intention relationship, while risk perception has no mediating effect. Finally, the study found the intergenerational factors (Baby Boomer, X, Y, and Z) have no moderating role on the relationships between return and risk perceptions on investment decisions. The result indicates that enhancing reinvestment intention in the Islamic capital market requires proper decision making by correctly perceived return and risk regardless intergeneration.

articleTitle: Green Reputation and Financial Performance in the Oil and Gas Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The current study aims to explore the relationship between environmental practices, social practices, and a firm's financial performance via green reputation. A qualitative literature review-based methodology was employed to dig out the prior literature and delved variables and relevant propositions. Previous literature reveals that both environmental and social practices are positive and significantly correlated with financial performance. Furthermore, prior literature also reveals the crucial role of green reputation between environmental practices, social practices, and financial performance to complete an underlying mechanism.

articleTitle: The Role of Cash Flow Sensitivity in Shaping Investment Strategies Across GCC Countries
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The current study examines the relationship between investment sensitivity and cash flow, with a particular focus on how capital market imperfections influence this sensitivity in GCC countries. Drawing on data from 100 publicly listed energy and non-financial companies, the research employs robust analytical and econometric methods, including a fixed-effects model for panel data spanning 2018 to 2023. Two regression models are utilized: the first examines the sensitivity of investment to cash flow across both sectors, while the second assesses the influence of capital market imperfections on this relationship. Key findings reveal that energy companies tend to be larger than their non-financial counterparts. At a 5% significance level, cash flow exerts a significant positive effect on investment sensitivity in both sectors. Moreover, a reduction in capital market imperfections corresponds with a decrease in the sensitivity of investment to cash flow. These results suggest that heightened investment sensitivity to cash flow reflects a tendency for firms to curtail investments when external financing is constrained, potentially hindering national economic growth. Based on these findings, the study advocates for targeted interventions. Policymakers are urged to implement micro-level initiatives aimed at enhancing corporate efficiency and macro-level strategies designed to strengthen financial markets, thereby fostering a more resilient economic environment.

articleTitle: Institutional Investment Effect to Investment Efficiency with External Audit Quality as Moderating Variable in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: To increase the owner's company's value, effective investment is required. To investigate the link between institutional investors and investment efficiency, this study looks into the experience of the company's external auditors. Fixed effect regression analysis is used in the study to examine Indonesian companies between 2018 and 2022. According to this study, the presence of certified auditors who are specialized enhances the bond between institutional investors and the investment effectiveness of the business. Qualified auditors' financial statements will lessen information asymmetry, strengthening institutional investors' supervisory duties in relation to investment efficiency. According to this study, a company's investment efficiency is significantly impacted by institutional investors that have an insurance-like emphasis, and the sort of investment management that is under the supervision of certified auditors has a substantial influence as well.

articleTitle: Literature Review of Digital Transformation on Banking: Corporate Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This research focus on discussing the extent of the impact of digital transformation on the performance of the banking industry in corporate area. In addition, this research will contribute to describing the development of digital transformation occurring in the banking industry and future research directions. This research uses a bibliometric approach to identify and map research trends in the latest era using PRISMA diagrams and VOS viewer. This research contributes to a clear measuring tool for digital transformation using the Index of Digital Transformation. Our findings also show that there is a research gap that exists between several studies that form the basis, so that in the future these variables can be tested for the development of new research models. Future research directions show that Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG), credit risk, agency costs, and industrial banking factors can be developed as main considerations.

articleTitle: Purchasing Decision of Halal Cosmetic Products Among Gen Z
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Gen Z is a consumer group increasingly aware of the importance of compliance with religious values and principles, including choosing halal cosmetic products. With the current high level of Generation Z, cosmetic businesses can protect their sustainability by concentrating on the variables that impact their purchasing decisions. The purpose of this study is to examine the elements that impact Gen Z consumers' purchase decisions for halal cosmetic product. This study employed a quantitative technique, delivering an online questionnaire with 25 statements and a five-point Likert scale. This survey included 400 respondents who use halal cosmetic products in Indonesia. The obtained data were then evaluated with PLS-SEM analysis using SmartPLS software. The study's findings show that religiosity, transparent product knowledge, effective advertising, and halal labeling on items all have a substantial impact on customer purchase decisions. In comparison to other variables, advertising has the biggest influence on purchasing decisions. A successful and focused advertising plan has the potential to significantly impact consumer preferences and urge them to make purchases. A better understanding of consumer preferences and efforts to build strong relationships with related communities can help companies positively influence purchasing decisions.

articleTitle: Integrating Machine Learning to Predict Entrepreneurial Success in Bahrain
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: In this paper, a new theoretical framework that integrates five theories into one model been proposed to predict entrepreneurial success-Psychological Traits Theory, Human Capital Theory, Social Capital Theory, Institutional Theory, and Resource-Based Theory. If we combine the aforementioned theories, it will provide us a better understating about the success of Entrepreneurs in Bahrain. The research proposed a theoretical framework combining all these theories and by utilizing machine learning such as decision tree model and other models we may achieve prediction of Entrepreneur in Bahrain. Entrepreneurial intentions and success have been discussed based on these theories and research hypotheses that have been developed. The idea to come up with predictive model that can be used by Entrepreneurs, lenders, Investors and policy makers to make a better-informed decision about startup which may lead to have a better eco system for Entrepreneurs in Bahrain.

articleTitle: Future Trends in Quantitative Finance and Algorithmic Trading Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The last several decades have witnessed tremendous changes in algorithmic trading and quantitative finance due to advances in data analytics, computing capacity, and technology. This study examines how these industries will evolve in the future while providing a thorough overview of recent advancements and upcoming trends. The paper starts with a historical review that traces the development of algorithmic trading methods and quantitative finance, emphasizing significant turning points and technical innovations. We examine the latest developments in high-frequency trading (HFT), the use of big data analytics, and the fusion of artificial intelligence and machine learning as they relate to quantitative finance. The study looks at a number of algorithmic trading techniques, including as sentiment-based trading, statistical arbitrage, trend following, mean reversion, and market creating. The potential for developing technologies to transform financial markets and trading methods is also taken into account, including the influence of blockchain, quantum computing, and sophisticated data visualization tools.

articleTitle: Understanding Generation Z's Interest in Sharia Fintech: The Roles of Usability, Benefits, and Security Perceptions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study investigates the factors influencing Generation Z's interest in utilizing Sharia fintech in Banda Aceh. It explores perceived ease of use, perceived benefits, and perceived security, emphasizing their roles in driving engagement with Sharia-compliant financial services. The results reveal that ease of use significantly affects interest in Sharia fintech, as younger users prioritize user-friendly interfaces and seamless navigation. Additionally, the perceived benefits, including ethical considerations and interest-free transactions, resonate with Generation Z's values, enhancing their engagement with Sharia fintech. Perceived security also plays a crucial role, as trust in data protection and secure transactions is vital for encouraging adoption among tech-savvy users. These findings provide valuable insights for fintech developers and Islamic financial institutions to create appealing Sharia fintech solutions tailored to the needs of Generation Z. Understanding these factors can lead to improved marketing strategies and product development, ultimately enhancing the adoption of Sharia fintech in the region.

articleTitle: The Effects of Halal Labels on Packaged Ice Cream Purchase Interest Among Foreign Muslim Consumers - A Case Study in Taiwan
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study explores the impact of halal labels on the purchase interest of foreign Muslim consumers in Taiwan, focusing on packaged ice cream. A total of 92 respondents from 11 different nationalities participated in the survey, providing insights into how halal certification influences consumer behavior in a non-Muslim majority country. The research used a mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative data from structured questionnaires and qualitative insights from interviews. The findings indicate a strong positive correlation (p = 0.985, p < 0.001) between the presence of halal labels and consumers' purchase intentions. Halal labels act as a key factor in building trust and encouraging the purchase of ice cream among Muslim consumers. The study highlights the importance of halal certification not only as a religious requirement but also as a marker of quality, safety, and ethical production standards. These insights are crucial for businesses and policymakers aiming to tap into the growing halal market in Taiwan.

articleTitle: Dynamic Volatility Interactions Between Sustainable Crypto Currencies and Green Economy Indicators
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: As the importance of sustainable development increases, firms and investors are increasingly interested in sustainable/green practices. The clean energy index, green bonds, and sustainable crypto applications are among them. In this study, the four most important sustainable crypto assets and the S&P Global Clean Energy Index and S&P Green Bond Index variables are used. Applying the Dynamically Correlated Multivariate Stochastic Volatility with Multivariate Volatility (DC-MSV) model, we observed that the S&P Global Clean Energy Index, S&P Green Index, Cordano, Bitgreen, Ripple, and Stellar variables exhibit intense volatility clustering and their volatilities are predictable. These findings are important for the selection of crypto assets to be added to the portfolio and risk management.

articleTitle: Magnifying the Nexus Between Adoption of Renewable Energy and Environmental Performance of Manufacturing Sector in Pakistan
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Environmental pollution has become an immense threat to humanity as it brings various natural climates such as drought, floods, and respiratory diseases which undermine human well-being. Stakeholders are forcing organizations to make their processes, operations, and functions more eco-friendly to enhance environmental performance by adopting environment-friendly means and technologies. Therefore, this study aims to examine the factors that affect the adoption of renewable energy and its nexus with environmental performance in the manufacturing sector of Pakistan. The structured close-ended questionnaire was distributed to senior managers of different organizations of the manufacturing sector. Data for this study was obtained from 218 respondents which were used for the analysis. A Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) statistical tool was employed to analyze the data. The results reveal that green self-efficacy is significantly and positively related to environmental performance and the adoption of renewable technology. Nevertheless, environmental awareness was found to be an insignificant predictor of environmental performance, while environmental awareness was positively related to the adoption of renewal technology. Adoption of renewable technology emerged as a significant predictor between green self-efficacy, green awareness, and environmental performance. Finally, it is also found that green strategy strengthens the relationship between renewable technology and environmental performance. It implies that when organizations formulate and implement green strategy (environment friendly initiatives and courses of action), they are more inclined towards adoption of renewable energy which consequently enhance better environmental performance by reducing negative footprint of manufacturing organizations.

articleTitle: Herding Under Asymmetric Market Stress: COVID-19 Impact on Indonesia's Sharia Stock Market
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study investigates herding behavior within Indonesia's Sharia-compliant stock market under asymmetric market stress during the COVID-19 pandemic. The research examines stocks listed on the Jakarta Islamic Index (JII), using daily data across three distinct periods: pre-crisis (January 2, 2019 - December 31,2019), crisis (January 2,2020 - December 31,2022), and post-crisis (January 2, 2023 - December 31,2023). Cross-sectional absolute deviation (CSAD) is employed to detect herding behavior. The results show that market volatility, measured by CSAD, peaked during the crisis period, with herding behavior becoming more evident. This behavior is attributed to heightened market uncertainty during the pandemic, where investors exhibited a tendency to follow the majority. In the post-crisis period, a gradual stabilization in market conditions is observed. These findings provide significant insights into investor behavior in Sharia stock markets under asymmetric stress, particularly during global financial crises like the COVID-19 pandemic.

articleTitle: The Interconnectedness Between Cryptocurrencies and Stock Markets in GCC Countries: An Empirical Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The GCC region has emerged as a hub for cryptocurrency innovation attracting investors globally, showcasing the region's commitment to fostering a vibrant digital economy. The marked increase in the investment in cryptocurrencies in the region in recent times is driven by many factors including a tech-savvy population, a supportive regulatory environment, the adoption of blockchain technology, and the like. The shift in investor's preference towards these cryptocurrencies as against traditional asset classes calls for a clear understanding between these two asset classes. Towards that end, this research examines the inter-dependencies between the cryptocurrencies and stock markets in Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries. The study analyzes a comprehensive dataset including ten cryptocurrencies and 6 stock market indices covering daily closing prices from 2020 to 2024. Granger causality tests and Lagrange multiplier autocorrelation parameters evaluate the dependencies and predictive linkages between stock indices and cryptocurrency prices. Preliminary findings reveal varying degrees of correlation, with Bitcoin and Ethereum exhibiting stronger links to GCC indices, likely reflecting their interdependency in the market.

articleTitle: Digitalization of Accountability in Philantrophy: The Missing Attention on Islamic-Based Organizations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study reviews the existing literature on the digitalization of accountability within Islamic-based philanthropic organizations, highlighting a significant gap in existing literature and practice. As digital technologies transform the landscape of philanthropy, Islamic organizations face unique challenges and opportunities in enhancing transparency and accountability. Despite the growing adoption of digital tools across the philanthropic sector, the specific implications for Islamic-based organizations remain underexplored. This research reviews existing studies in the field, identifies key studies highlighting the issue, and identifies a literature gap in the digitalization of accountability within Islamic-based philanthropic organizations. It is noted that the importance of tailored digital strategies that align with both technological advancements and Islamic values, offering practical recommendations for enhancing the accountability practices of Islamic philanthropic organizations. Ultimately, this research aims to contribute to a more robust understanding of issues in digital accountability within the broader field of philanthropy and emphasizing the need for more studies to be performed in relation to Islamic philanthropy organizations.

articleTitle: Enhancing Compliance and Efficiency in Islamic Banking through RegTech Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: A tsunami of new laws was enacted in the banking industry as a result of the financial crisis. Since then, it has become increasingly important to consider how financial institutions can maintain compliance with this constantly growing financial legal framework. The prospective use of RegTech solutions to assure legal compliance is examined in this presentation. RegTech is the application of technology to simplify compliance with and oversight of regulatory obligations. RegTech is nearly universally praised in modern legal doctrine as bearing the prospect of significant gains in terms of improved efficiency and less risk of human errors and ensuing administrative fines. Finally, this article highlights the critical function of the financial supervisor in the RegTech age as a liaison between legislators and financial institutions. RegTech does speed up the transition to a cooperative supervision model where the supervisor supports financial institutions in their quest for adequate and accurate compliance and where financial institutions provide supervisors with crucial input for the creation of effective standards, best practices, and RegTech solutions.
